[center][color=#990000][b]*** JUDGEMENT HOUSE 2004: October 29, 30 & 31! [[evangelicalsintl.org/judgement|Get your tickets]] ***[/b][/color]
[color=#990000]Fall Fellowship Potluck is Saturday![/color]

You are visitor number [b]004127[/b] since March 1999![/center]

Welcome, friend! Evangelicals International was founded in 1977 by our Senior Pastor, {{Elias Crane|name}}, in a living room on Harrow Lane. Today we are a family of more than 600 members, worshipping at the Mother Church at 412 Harrow Lane.

[b]Service Times[/b]
Sunday Worship ... 10:00 AM
Wednesday Fellowship ... 7:00 PM
Neighborhood Prayer Watch ... nightly, members only

We believe a church family should also be a family in business, in housing, and in every part of life. Please support the [[evangelicalsintl.org/directory|businesses of our church family]]!

Is the enemy working in YOUR neighborhood? Learn the warning signs with our [[evangelicalsintl.org/warfare|Spiritual Warfare Ministry]].

[b]This Week at the Mother Church[/b]
  - Sunday: Pastor Crane preaches "The Tidy House" (Matthew 12:44)
  - Tuesday: "Satan in Suburbia" with Deputy Drury, Fellowship Hall
  - Wednesday: Youth Group, pizza and Bible trivia with Sister Lydia
  - Thursday: {{Harvest Fellowship|org}} ([[harvestfellowship.net|web site]]) at [[mcc.edu/clubs|Millbrook Community College]]. Bring a friend who needs work!
  - Saturday: Fall Fellowship Potluck. [[home.millnet.com/~bgunderson|Barb Gunderson's]] raffle quilt will be drawn at 7!

New to Millbrook? Our Welcome Ministry would love to visit your home! Just leave your address in our [[evangelicalsintl.org/guestbook|guestbook]], and let us know whether you own or rent so we can pray for you properly.

pages.body:
Evangelicals International is a non-denominational congregation and a registered non-profit religious corporation. Our Senior Pastor has shepherded this family for twenty-seven years.

Since 1985 our [[evangelicalsintl.org/warfare|Spiritual Warfare Ministry]] has stood between Millbrook's families and the enemy.

In 1998 our Pastor endured a season of trial, and our family stood with him. We came through it stronger.

Our church owns no property. All of our buildings are generously provided by {{Crane Holdings LLC|org}}, a private company, at no cost to our members.

The church is governed by a [[evangelicalsintl.org/board|Board of Directors]] of ten men, who serve without pay.

[b]Our Ministries[/b]
  - The [[evangelicalsintl.org/warfare|Neighborhood Prayer Watch]] (nightly)
  - Harvest Fellowship at Millbrook Community College (Thursdays)
  - Retreats and deliverance counseling at the [[pinehollowestates.com/lodge|Pine Hollow Lodge]]
  - [[evangelicalsintl.org/judgement|Judgement House]], every October since 1987

[b]Our History[/b]
Our church first met in a living room on Harrow Lane. In 1977 our Pastor bought the old Grange Hall at 412 Harrow Lane "for a song" from the last members of {{Harrow Grange No. 212|org}}. He still keeps the Grange's charter framed in his office. He says it reminds him who was here first.

pages.title: Local preacher sentenced in charity fraud (June 1998)
pages.body:
Elias Crane, 44, pastor of a small Harrow Lane congregation, was sentenced Tuesday to three years for diverting $212,000 in donations from the {{Harrow Lane Food Pantry|org}} into accounts he controlled.

The pantry's bookkeeper, {{Miriam Hale|name}}, testified against Crane in exchange for immunity. Prosecutors said Hale's handwritten ledgers were the heart of the case.

Outside the courthouse, Crane told reporters: "The Lord keeps better books than the county."

Crane's attorney, paid for by his congregation, argued that the pantry's records were "incomplete." The judge disagreed, calling Hale's ledgers "the most complete financial records this court has ever seen from a church."

Hale was granted immunity and was not charged. The pantry's outside auditor, {{Aldous Vole|name}}, CPA, told the court he had "no reason to suspect anything" in five years of annual audits.

The {{Harrow Lane Food Pantry|org}} has suspended operations.

pages.title: Residents fume over late-night tows (November 2003)
pages.body:
Harrow Lane residents say their cars are being towed at 3 and 4 in the morning for missing "service stickers" required by their homeowners association.

The tows are performed by Coyle Auto Repair & Towing. Driver {{Abel Coyle|name}} declined to comment. Fees to recover a vehicle start at $385, cash only.

The {{Harrow Lane Homeowners Association|org}} defends the policy. "Service stickers keep unsafe vehicles off our street," said Association secretary Lydia Greaves. Asked what service the sticker represents, Greaves said, "Compliance."

Coyle's tow yard is on Route 9, next to the Pine Hollow turnoff. It is open Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10 AM to noon. The company is listed in the [[evangelicalsintl.org/directory|business directory]] of Evangelicals International.

pages.title: Harrow Lane church keeps doors open in pastor's absence (April 1999)
pages.body:
Ten months after its pastor went to prison, the congregation at 412 Harrow Lane is still meeting every Sunday, and its food pantry reopened last week.

{{Paul Rennick|name}}, 44, a science teacher at Millbrook High School and a member since 1985, has led services since Elias Crane's sentencing. He says the pantry now publishes its books every quarter.

"Every can is counted," Rennick said. "Every dollar is on paper where anyone can see it."

Asked whether Crane would be welcomed back, Rennick said that was a question for the congregation.

Former bookkeeper Miriam Hale no longer volunteers at the pantry. Rennick said the congregation "wishes her well."

The new quarterly reports are audited by the same outside firm as before, [[bizsearch.sos.gov/vole-cpa|Vole & Associates]]. "Aldous did the audits before, too," Rennick said. "We've asked him to look harder this time."

The pantry is open Saturdays, 9 AM to noon.

pages.title: Crane returns to Harrow Lane pulpit (August 2001)
pages.body:
Elias Crane preached Sunday for the first time since his release from state prison, to a crowd that spilled onto Harrow Lane.

The congregation, now calling itself Evangelicals International, says it has nearly tripled in size since 1998. A new board of directors has been named.

Board chair Paul Rennick, who led the church during Crane's sentence, said he would stay on the board "as long as the books stay open." Crane did not take questions.

Among those welcoming Crane back was {{Miriam Hale|name}}, the pantry bookkeeper whose testimony helped convict him. "Everyone deserves a second book," she told the Ledger, then corrected herself: "A second chance."

The new board includes local business owners Walter Greaves, Isaac Mercer and Levi Strand. Two more seats will be filled "as the Lord provides," according to a statement from the church.

Several congregants in the front pews said afterward that the Pastor's voice seemed to come "from much lower than a man's chest." One woman said the lights over the pulpit dimmed each time he raised his hands. That summer the church replaced its red EXIT signs with green ones.

pages.title: Letters: Harrow Lane is being bought one fine at a time (September 2004)
pages.body:
To the editor:

I have lived at 413 Harrow Lane for twenty-one years. This summer my homeowners association began fining me $150 a day for a light. The light is a red observing lamp in my backyard, and it is the dimmest light on the street.

My tenant's car was towed at three in the morning from in front of her own home. My other house has been cited for a fence, a mailbox and my grass. I have received three offers to buy all of it. They came from the same company, and that company is at the end of my street.

I am paying the fines, and I will keep paying them, because I know how these men work. I used to sit at their table.

Paul Rennick
Harrow Lane

[color=#666666][i]Editor's note: The Harrow Lane Homeowners Association was offered space to respond. Secretary Lydia Greaves said the Association "does not comment on disparagement," and added that Mr. Rennick has been fined under Section 12.4 of the covenants for writing this letter.[/i][/color]

pages.title: Observing Log, Fall 2004
pages.body:
[b]09/12[/b]  Seeing 2/5. Excavator running behind 412 again at 2 AM. Called the Sheriff. Nobody came that I saw.

[b]09/24[/b]  Seeing 4/5. M31 beautiful. At 3:10 a man was standing on my lawn about ten feet from the shed, not speaking, not moving, just facing the house. I went inside and called. By the time Drury's cruiser came up the street he was gone. Drury didn't get out of the car.

[b]09/30[/b]  Clouded out. Fine notice number 61 came today, for the red lamp. Paid it.

[b]10/02[/b]  They towed Rosa's car. Gave her the $385. She asked if she should move. I said that's her choice. She said, whose?

[b]10/08[/b]  Seeing 3/5, but at 3:15 exactly the image started shaking, and it was coming up through the pier. I'd blame traffic if there were ever any traffic on Harrow at 3:15.

[b]10/11[/b]  The Kettering girl is back in the parked car across the street with a notebook. Couldn't be more than eighteen. She waved. I waved back. I wonder if they tell her what the notebook is for.

[b]10/12[/b]  The young man next door at 411 was up at three again, blue screen in his back window. Turns out he writes for the Ledger. Told him to read my letter. Told him to start with the pantry.

[b]10/13[/b]  Letter from my bank. My mortgage was sold. I know who bought it. I wish Miriam had kept her copy.

[b]10/14[/b]  Clear. Bill's seismometer is on the pier. A spike at 3:15:00 and another at 3:15:40. Two pulses, like knocking. Printed the trace for the club.

[b]10/14, 3:20 AM[/b]  Switched the red lamp off for a minute to change the battery. The second pulse came early, hard enough to rattle the eyepiece case. I switched it back on and the shaking stopped mid-shake. For twenty years I've told myself Wendell was a superstitious old man.

[b]10/14, later[/b]  Someone is photographing my shed from the church lot. I waved, and this time nobody waved back. The Kettering girl wasn't in the car tonight, which I hope means something good.

pages.title: HAVE YOU SEEN RUTH?
pages.body:
[center][b][color=#990000]HAVE YOU SEEN RUTH?[/color][/b][/center]

{{Ruth Pell|name}}, 19. Brown hair, brown eyes, 5'4". Small scar on her left thumb from a canning jar.

Ruth moved to Pine Hollow Estates, north of Millbrook, in June 2004. She has not called, written or e-mailed since. Her friends have not heard from her.

The Sheriff says Ruth is an adult and may live wherever she chooses. I understand that. I only want to hear her voice.

If you work at the Pine Hollow Lodge, or deliver there, or have seen her, please write to me. You do not have to give your name.

[b]Update 10/07:[/b] I drove to the gate on Wednesday. I was given a trespass warning. The deputy who wrote it has eaten at my table.

-- Esther Pell, epell@millnet.com

[b]Things Ruth Loves[/b] (in case you see her)
Strawberry jam, Amy Grant, her old blue Bible with the broken zipper, and the barn cats at her grandmother's. If you mention any of these, she will know you talked to me.

[b]Update 10/12:[/b] A deputy came to my door to ask whether I ever "took Ruth to meetings in the woods" when she was little. I asked what he meant. He said there was a report. I have taken Ruth to the woods exactly once, for a Brownie campout in 1992, and it rained.

[b]Update 10/14:[/b] A girl sat in a car outside [[millbrooklutheran.org|Grace Lutheran]] during our Tuesday circle. I knocked and offered her coffee. She said no, very politely. She looked like she wanted to say something else. If you are reading this, dear, the offer stands.

Hi! I'm Barbara T. Gunderson (Barb!) and I've been quilting for 31 years. My granddaughter set up this page for me so bear with me!!

[b]Current Project[/b]
A raffle quilt for the Fall Potluck at the church on Harrow Lane. The ladies gave me the pattern: a big five-pointed star, point DOWN, with a little candle at each point and each place the lines cross. Ten candles. Eight in gold thread and two left blank. I said Lydia, isn't that star upside down? Isn't that one of the signs from Deputy Drury's seminar? She laughed and said I'd understand later. Well OK! It's their raffle.

[b]MillNet Tech Support FAQ[/b]
[color=#666666]Updated 10/12/2004[/color]

[b]Q: I get a busy signal when I dial in.[/b]
A: Evenings between 7 and 10 PM are our busiest time. Please try again later, or ask about our new Night Owl plan ($14.95/mo, midnight to 6 AM only).

[b]Q: How do I set up my e-mail in Outlook Express?[/b]
A: Incoming server: mail.millnet.com. Outgoing: smtp.millnet.com. Your password is on the sticker on your install CD.

[b]Q: Can I get DSL?[/b]
A: DSL is coming to Millbrook in 2005! Probably!

[b]Q: My little brother picked up the phone and now I'm disconnected.[/b]
A: That will do it.

[b]Q: Why does my connection drop at 3:15 AM? (Harrow Lane customers)[/b]
A: We have tested all lines serving the Harrow Lane area and found no fault.

[color=#999999]I went out to the Harrow junction pedestal on 10/10 at 3 AM with the line tester. The line itself is clean. Whatever the noise is, it's in the conduit, or in the ground around the conduit. At 3:15 the needle went all the way over and the pedestal was warm to the touch in 40 degree weather. I could hear something through the case, like someone breathing through a paper towel tube a long way off. I'm not going out there again at night, so please stop calling about this. We can't fix it, because it isn't ours. -Rick[/color]

[b]Q: A pop-up says I've been "flagged by the Watch." What do I do?[/b]
A: That is a pop-up ad. Do not click it. Also, please stop calling Rick at home.

[b]Q: Is MillNet Y2K compliant?[/b]
A: It is 2004.

[b]Q: Who is dialup-217?[/b]
A: We don't give out customer information. [color=#999999](Several people have asked this week. One said she was from the HOA. We don't give out customer information to the HOA either. -Rick)[/color]

pages.title: Harrow Grange No. 212: A History
pages.body:
[center][b]HARROW GRANGE No. 212[/b]
A History, by Clarence Oyler
Millbrook Historical Society
[color=#990000]PHOTOS COMING SOON![/color][/center]

[b]Founding[/b]
The Harrow Grange was chartered on June 21, 1911 by nine farm families of the Harrow Lane district. The hall was raised that summer on the site of the old Harrow spring, which the charter calls "the Well." The brick cistern beneath the hall was already there when they built. No one I have spoken to knows who laid it.

[b]Grange Life[/b]
For sixty years the Grange was the heart of the district: dances, the fall fair, the lending library, the 4-H. My brother Wendell and I went to our first dance there in 1927.

[b]The Officers' Lamps[/b]
Most Granges have one Gate Keeper. Harrow Grange had ten Keepers, each with a brass lamp, and each assigned to a household on the lane. The lamps were lit every night, on a schedule kept in a book that never left the hall. The schedule was called the Watch. Visiting Grangers from Olympia found this very odd and said so in their letters.

[b]Hallowe'en 1931[/b]
On the night of October 31, 1931, four of the officers held a meeting in the lower room without the others. The minutes for October 1931 are missing. The minutes for November record only that "the lower room is closed by vote, and the Watch is ended." Every officer resigned that winter. Harlan Strand, who was found in the cistern the next morning, lived eleven more years in a back bedroom on Harrow Lane. He never spoke again, and his family kept every lamp in that house lit, day and night, until he died. Tobias Drury was never found. When I asked Wendell about it he got up and left the table. He has not discussed it since.

[b]The End of the Grange[/b]
Membership dwindled after the war. The last meeting was held June 21, 1974. The cistern was bricked over by vote of the final members, at their own expense. In 1977 the hall was sold to a young man who had been holding prayer meetings in his living room down the street and wanted room to grow.

[b]A Local Custom[/b]
Old families on Harrow Lane used to say the Grange "kept the lid on." When I asked on what, they said the Well, and laughed, and changed the subject. If you know, please write to me.

[b]The Keepers' Book[/b]
The Watch schedule was kept in a leather book that never left the hall. I am told it was not destroyed in 1974 but stayed with the building when it was sold. If the church on Harrow Lane still has it, I would dearly like to see it. I have written to their pastor twice. He has not answered.

[b]The Ten Households[/b]
From the 1920 Grange roll, the Keepers' households were: Oyler, Pruitt, Strand, Coyle, Drury, Hale, Mercer, Pell, Finch and Kettering. The Oylers kept the red lamp. Several of these names are still on the lane.

[color=#666666]Page created 03/1996. Last updated 11/1996. Photos coming soon!
[font_size=12][i]Note, 1998: Clarence passed away in December 1997. We will keep his page up as he left it. -- Millbrook Historical Society[/i][/font_size][/color]

pages.title: Obituaries: October 2004
pages.body:
[b]Wendell James Oyler[/b], 94
Wendell Oyler, the last surviving member of Harrow Grange No. 212, died October 10 at [[millbrookcarecenter.com|Millbrook Care Center]]. Born on a farm on Harrow Lane in 1910, he worked forty years for the county roads department. He was preceded in death by his wife Irene and his brother Clarence, a local historian. He is survived by a grandson, Ron, of Millbrook.
Services will be private. In lieu of flowers, the family asks that the lamps be left lit.

[b]Dorothy Anne Lund[/b], 88
Dorothy Lund died peacefully at home October 7. A founding member of the Millbrook Tuesday Bridge Club, she won the county championship in 1963, 1971 and 1988, and never let anyone forget it. Memorial gifts to the Millbrook Public Library.

[b]Gerald "Gary" Pruitt[/b], 71
Gary Pruitt carried mail in Millbrook for 31 years, most of them on the Harrow Lane route. He liked to say he could tell every house on Harrow by its porch light. He is survived by his daughter, Lydia Greaves, and by his model trains, which he left to his son-in-law Walter. Services Saturday at Evangelicals International, 412 Harrow Lane.

[b]Ingrid Halvorsen[/b], 90
Ingrid Halvorsen, mother of pumpkin champion "Big Gene" Halvorsen, died October 12. She taught piano to three generations of Millbrook children, most of whom still cannot play "Fur Elise" all the way through. Services at [[millbrooklutheran.org|Grace Lutheran]].

[color=#999999]Correction: The obituary for Wendell Oyler should have said that he is also survived by "the lamps he kept." The family asked that this be printed exactly as written.[/color]

The county has closed {{Little Lambs Home Daycare|org}} at 405 Harrow Lane after several parents made what a sheriff's spokesman called "allegations of a ritualistic nature" against its owner, {{Carol Lindqvist|name}}, 38.

The allegations surfaced after a Halloween prayer meeting at the church on Harrow Lane, where Sunday school teacher {{Joan Finch|name}} had been "helping the little ones talk about their bad dreams," according to one parent.

Deputy {{Daniel Drury|name}}, who has lectured locally on occult crime, said the case bore "every hallmark" of organized Satanism. Asked for physical evidence, Drury said: "These people are very, very good at hiding it."

Lindqvist, who has run the daycare for nine years, has not been charged. Her attorney called the claims "a moral panic with a church potluck attached."

Parents say the children's accounts grew more detailed over several weeks of sessions with Mrs. Finch. "At first my son just said he had a bad dream," one mother said. "Now he remembers candles. And a room under the ground."

Little Lambs has operated at 405 Harrow Lane since 1977. Its license was suspended Friday pending investigation.

pages.title: Charges dropped against daycare owner (March 1988)
pages.body:
The county prosecutor has dropped all charges against Carol Lindqvist, the former owner of Little Lambs Home Daycare, after sixteen months and no physical evidence.

Lindqvist no longer lives in Millbrook. Her home at 405 Harrow Lane was sold last fall to cover legal costs. County records list the buyer as {{Crane Holdings LLC|org}}, a company registered in 1987.

Deputy Daniel Drury, who led the investigation, said he was "disappointed but not surprised." "The absence of evidence is how you know they're good at it," he said.

Rev. Elias Crane, whose congregation held prayer vigils outside the daycare throughout 1987, declined to comment, but sent the Ledger a tract titled "Is Your Neighbor a Satanist?"

Lindqvist's attorney said his client will not sue. "She wants to be left alone," he said. "She asked me to say that she forgives the children. She has not said anything about the adults."

Deputy Drury said he will expand his occult crime seminar at the church on Harrow Lane into a monthly series beginning in May.

pages.title: Editorial: We owe Carol Lindqvist an apology (October 1991)
pages.body:
Five years ago this month, this newspaper ran eleven front-page stories about "satanic ritual abuse" at a Harrow Lane daycare. We quoted a sheriff's deputy, a Sunday school teacher and a pastor. We did not quote a single piece of evidence, because there was none.

Carol Lindqvist lost her business, her house and her good name. The people who accused her lost nothing. One of them bought her house.

We did not ask who benefited. We should have. We owe Ms. Lindqvist an apology, and we are making it here, too late to matter.

The Ledger has also learned that three of the families who accused Ms. Lindqvist now rent their homes from the same company that bought hers. We do not yet know what that means. We intend to find out.

-- The Editors

[color=#999999][i]Note, 2004: We never did. The reporter assigned to the story, Ben Talley, died in 1992 when his car left Route 9 near the Pine Hollow turnoff. Coyle Auto towed the wreck. -- D.R.[/i][/color]

pages.title: Harrow Lane lamps dark on Hallowe'en; Grange officers silent (November 1931)
pages.body:
[color=#666666][font_size=12]From the Millbrook Ledger, Tuesday, November 3, 1931. Transcribed from microfilm by the Millbrook Historical Society.[/font_size][/color]

Residents of the Harrow Lane district report that the ten lamps kept by the officers of Harrow Grange No. 212 were not lit on Saturday night last, Hallowe'en, for the first time in memory.

Several farm families on the lane say they were woken after three o'clock in the morning by what one described as "a sound like the whole valley drawing breath."

Mr. {{Wendell Oyler|name}}, 21, the youngest of the Grange's Keepers, would say only that it was "Grange business" and that his own lamp "was lit, whatever the others did."

Four officers of the Grange, Messrs. E. Pruitt, H. Strand, J. Coyle and T. Drury, have declined to speak with this paper.

On Sunday morning Mr. {{Harlan Strand|name}} was found at the bottom of the dry cistern beneath the Grange hall, where he appears to have lain through the night. Dr. Amundsen says Mr. Strand's injuries are "not of a kind I have seen from a fall" and does not expect him to recover. Mr. Pruitt and Mr. Coyle, who were with him that evening, say they "believed he had gone home."

Mr. {{Tobias Drury|name}} has not been seen since Saturday night. His brass lamp was recovered from the cistern. Sheriff Lund reports that its glass had melted inward, "as if from a great heat on the outside." Mrs. Drury asks the public for any word of her husband.

[b]Also on the lane[/b]: Mrs. Hale reports that her hens have stopped laying. Mr. Pell's dog has not come home. The Grange asks residents to keep their doors shut after dark until further notice.

The Grange has cancelled its Thanksgiving dance.

pages.title: Harrow Grange holds its last meeting (June 1974)
pages.body:
Harrow Grange No. 212 held its final meeting Friday night, sixty-three years to the day after its charter. Eleven members attended.

By a vote of 11 to 0, the members agreed to pay out of their own pockets to brick over the old cistern beneath the hall before the building is sold. A county surveyor who inspected the cistern last month reported a brick passage running east from it, under Harrow Lane, "of considerable age and unknown extent." The members asked that the passage be sealed as well.

"Some things you keep a lid on," said longtime member Wendell Oyler, 64. He declined to explain.

Members voting to seal the cistern included the Oyler, Pruitt, Hale and Pell families. The Strand, Coyle and Drury families were not present.

The Grange's records, including a book of officers' schedules that members call "the Watch," will stay with the hall.

The hall will be listed for sale this summer. The brass lamps of the Grange officers, a local curiosity, will be divided among the members' families.

Second Friday of the month at my house. Bring your own adhesive! My husband will be in his office doing somebody's taxes, so we can be as loud as we like.

Never store your best album where you live. Heat, water, little hands and husbands are all hazards. I keep my most precious album with someone I trust, who has never once asked to look inside it.

[center][b]THE BOOK OF THE WATCH[/b]
{{Harrow Grange No. 212|org}}
Kept by the Keepers. Not to leave the hall.[/center]

The Well was here before us, and the lid was here before us, and we are not the first to keep it.

What lives in the Well is the Beast that John saw rising up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns. It is not in the sea. It is under Harrow Lane, in the black water under the brick. It does not sleep. It waits for the lane to be given to it.

It cannot take what is not given. So it asks, and it asks through men. It will ask for a field, a house, a signature, a child. Every thing given to it is a door, and when there are ten doors it will come up through the Well in the body and take possession of the lane and all who live on it.

Therefore there are ten Keepers and ten lamps, one for each door. Each Keeper lights his lamp at dusk and watches his house until dawn, so that nothing on the lane is given in the dark.

[b]Of the red lamp.[/b] One lamp is glazed red. The Beast cannot abide red light. Under it He cannot walk, cannot speak into a man's ear, cannot move a hand that is not His own. He can only wait. The red lamp is kept by the Keeper nearest the Well. It is never to be put out. It is never to be sold, only given.

[b]Of the hour.[/b] He rises at a quarter past three, when the night is lowest. Listen for Him in the ground.

[color=#999999]-- Written for the Keepers by C. Hale, Master, June 21, 1911[/color]

[color=#999999]In pencil, a later hand: Received with the hall. Read with great interest. -- E.C., 1977[/color]

[b]Set down by W. Oyler, Keeper, the morning of November 1, 1931[/b]
Pruitt said the book was wrong. He said the Beast pays for what is given to Him, and pays well, and that four doors given together would be enough to bargain with. At midnight the four of them put out their lamps and went down to the lower room. I kept mine lit on the lane, as I was told to.

At a quarter past three the ground breathed in. Every dog on the lane went quiet at once.

They came up at four without Strand. Coyle's hands were burned black to the wrist. Pruitt would not look at me. I asked where Harlan was. Pruitt said, "He was given."

I went down with the red lamp. Harlan was in the bottom of the cistern with his eyes open. Where the red light touched him he began to scream, and I thank God for it, because it meant he was still alive. I could not find Tobias Drury. I found his lamp against the far wall, where the passage runs east under the lane. The glass had gone soft and run inward. Past it the brick was wet and warm, and I did not go on.

Four doors were not enough. I pray the Grange sees to it that there are never ten.

[color=#999999]In pencil, a later hand: Four were not enough because they were given in the dark, in a hurry, by frightened men. Ours will be given in daylight, in ink, before a notary. -- E.C., 2002[/color]

pages.title: How the Pastor came to the lane (locked)
pages.body:
[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
Walter tells me Levi has been asking whether I am "still myself." I will answer once, and only here.

In the spring of 1977 I bought a Grange hall with a hole under it. I was twenty-three years old, I had eleven people in my living room, and I wanted more. The book came with the hall. I read it the way you would read a warranty.

The first night I went down to the lower room alone, put my hands flat on the brick, and asked what it wanted, the way you would ask a man. Something answered from very far down. It said it wanted the lane. I asked what I would get. It showed me.

It came up into me that night, and it has been in me ever since. It is patient and it is very old and it is always, always cold.

Here is the part none of you three understand. It has never once made me do anything. It cannot. It can only offer. Every dollar I took from that pantry, every child Joan sat with, every deed Levi stamped, I chose, with my own hands, and I would choose them all again. That is why He picked me. A man who has to be forced is of no use to Him.

So yes, Levi, I am still myself, and that is the worst thing I can tell you.

[b]horn_vii[/b] wrote:
Thank you, Pastor.

pages.title: the true order, 10/31
pages.body:
[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
The order of service Miriam posted downstairs is the one the seven will see. This is the one that will happen.

  [b]11:30 PM[/b] ... The three from the wing go into the lower room. They will be calm. They are not there to be prayed over.
  [b]1:00 AM[/b] ... Ten deeds on the brick, laid by ten hands. Seven of those hands don't know what they're signing, and that is the point. A door has to be opened by the one who owns it.
  [b]2:00 AM[/b] ... Walter: 413's lamp is out by now, or 413 is. Daniel's will be the only car on Harrow.
  [b]3:00 AM[/b] ... I go down to the Well. Levi brings the Grange's red lamp up from the vault, and I break it on the brick myself.
  [b]3:15 AM[/b] ... The three are given.
  [b]After[/b] ... Whatever He asks for. If He asks for more, Amos wrote a policy on his own daughter in July and still doesn't know why I asked him to.
  [b]4:00 AM[/b] ... He rises, and takes possession of the lane and everyone on it.

[b]watchman[/b] wrote:
And the seven? When they come up at four and see what's in the cistern?

[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
They'll do what they've always done, Daniel. They'll decide it was the Lord's will, and they'll do the paperwork.

[b]watchman[/b] wrote:
And you, Pastor? After?

[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
I have been a tenant for twenty-seven years. After the 31st, He won't need a tenant.

pages.title: on holding Him
pages.body:
[b]watchman[/b] wrote:
I have spent eighteen years teaching this town what Satan looks like, and I never once had evidence. Now I have seen the real one. Nobody in Millbrook will be safe unless the men holding His leash are men who know what He is. After the 31st, we hold it. I'll point Him at the real evil in this county, and I will never need evidence again.

[b]horn_vii[/b] wrote:
My grandfather Harlan was left at the bottom of that cistern in 1931 by men who didn't do the paperwork. He lay in a back bedroom for eleven years with every lamp in the house burning. I do the paperwork. After the 31st, nothing on this lane changes hands again without my stamp, and nothing comes up out of that hole unless I've signed for it.

[b]horn_ii[/b] wrote:
Lydia's grandfather went down that night too, and he came back up. He lived to be ninety and never wanted for a thing, and neither has any Pruitt since. Whatever he was promised, I want the rest of it, for Lydia and for our children. And if somebody is going to hold this lane, better us than someone worse.

[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
Each of you believes you will be the one holding Him. That's good. Keep believing it until the 31st.

pages.title: the seven
pages.body:
[b]horn_ii[/b] wrote:
They believe they're the Lord's ten kings. Let them. A man who thinks he's holy will sign anything.

[b]horn_vii[/b] wrote:
Aldous found the old Grange book in the Pastor's office and asked me what the pencil notes mean.

[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
Aldous counts. He doesn't read. Tell him it's Grange nonsense.

[b]watchman[/b] wrote:
Amos asked downstairs why the Pastor goes down alone at 3. Samuel asked why nothing red. Isaac says his boy won't go into the round room anymore.

[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
The seven are the doors. They don't need to know they're doors. A door that knows it's a door starts to wonder who's knocking.

[b]horn_ii[/b] wrote:
And Miriam? She's read the book. All of it.

[b]E.C.[/b] wrote:
Miriam has been deciding whether to burn that other ledger for six years. Watch her. Don't touch her. She's the last one who can still choose.

  1. the hum: fundamental around 21 Hz. starts at 3:15:00, stops at 3:21:00. every night since at least 10/05.
  2. the seismometer: two pulses, 40 seconds apart. amplitude up about 12% every night. if it keeps growing at that rate, the two pulses merge into one on the night of 10/31. i did the math three times.
  3. the "voice" on owen's tape sits between 300 and 900 Hz. it drops out whenever the camcorder's red REC light faces the drain. so thursday night i went to the drain in front of 411 with my bike lights. red LED (about 630 nm) on the drain: voice gone. green LED: voice back, louder. white: same as nothing.
  4. paul switched his red lamp off for one minute on 10/14. bill's trace jumped.

sound shouldn't care what color a light is. i don't have a hypothesis, just a data set i don't like.

(the voice says "four one one, four one three." it's the same every night. it's getting clearer.)

pages.body:
[center][b]Carol's Quilt Room[/b]
Spokane, Washington
[color=#999999][image: log_cabin_border.gif][/color][/center]

Welcome! I've quilted since I was a girl. Mostly Log Cabin and Irish Chain. I teach a beginners' class at the Spokane library on Saturdays, and my sister's grandkids keep me busy the rest of the week.

[b]Current Project[/b]
A baby quilt for my great-niece, in yellows. No red. I don't use red anymore.

[b]An Open Letter[/b]
[color=#666666](posted 10/2004)[/color]
A young man from a college in Millbrook called me last week about a documentary. I told him I wouldn't go on camera. I've changed my mind about one thing: I want my own words somewhere, in case his film is never shown.

My name is {{Carol Lindqvist|name}}. From 1977 to 1986 I ran {{Little Lambs Home Daycare|org}} at 405 Harrow Lane. In 1985 Pastor Elias Crane came to my door twice to offer to buy my house. It was a corner lot, he said, and the church needed room to grow. I said no both times.

The next fall, Joan Finch began "helping" some of my children talk about their bad dreams. She held the sessions in the fellowship hall at 412. Within three weeks the children "remembered" candles and robes and a room under the ground. Deputy Drury told the newspaper I was very good at hiding things. I lost my license, then my savings to the lawyers, then my house. The company that bought it had existed for eleven days.

I forgive those children. They were four years old, and they said what the grown-ups needed them to say. Some of them rent Crane Holdings houses now, and I hope they're warm.

I have not forgiven the grown-ups, and I'm not sure I ever will.

One more thing, for whoever is looking into this now. The candles and the robes and the room under the ground were real. They just weren't mine, and those children didn't make them up. Somebody showed them. Ask who had the key to the lower room at 412 in the fall of 1986.

-- Carol

[color=#990000]This album is private.[/color] Photos are hidden. Captions are shown for the page owner.[/center]

[b]Page 1[/b] ... Thanksgiving 1997 at the pantry. 340 families!
[b]Page 2[/b] ... Paul and me counting cans. He counted everything twice, and so did I, only I wrote mine down in two different books.
[b]Pages 3 to 26[/b] ... [color=#999999](private)[/color] Book B, January 1993 to December 1997, photographed one page at a time.
[b]Page 27[/b] ... Every "rent" check the pantry wrote to Crane Holdings, 1993 to 1997. Total: $212,000. The court called it theft, but it was really a purchase.
[b]Page 28[/b] ... Book B isn't money. Elias had me keep it from the first week. Every family who ever came to the pantry, what they owned, and what they could be made to give. I thought it was a donor list. Then I read the Grange book, and I understood it's a list of doors.
[b]Page 29[/b] ... Where the real Book B is: with W.O., who kept a light on for me when no one else would. He has never once asked to look inside.
[b]Last page[/b] ... For Paul, if I never get the chance: I'm sorry I told the court there was only one book. There were always two. Elias took the first one and let the county have it. I kept the second. I have never been brave enough to do anything with it.
